D/F/J/K Rhythm Game Project
7th Grade Final Project
Second Trimester
Project Overview

You will complete, test, and present a D/F/J/K rhythm game in Scratch. This project combines programming, game design, testing, and explanation to create an interactive game that responds to keyboard input.
Learning Objectives
Identify the main sprites, variables, broadcasts, and loops in the rhythm game
Use D, F, J, and K keyboard inputs to control the game
Explain how targets, collisions, score, time, and tempo work together
Implement programming structures such as events, conditions, loops, and variables
Complete the target creation, movement, scoring, and missed-note systems
Use visual and sound feedback to communicate game results
Break down the game into manageable programming tasks
Examine how different scripts work together as one system
Test and refine the game for accurate and consistent behavior
Assess the effectiveness of the controls and feedback
Make one improvement based on testing results
Present the completed game and explain its main programming features
Project Plan
Starter Code - Part 1
Build the teacher-guided starter code and review the project requirements
Add the D, F, J, and K key sprites
Add the target sprites and starting positions
Create the score, time, and tempo variables
Add the main green-flag setup and first broadcasts
Save the starter project correctly
Check that each partner understands the completed parts
Prepare the project for testing
Starter Code Testing
Run the starter project and check the D, F, J, and K controls
Check variables, targets, and broadcasts
Record one error and the correction made
Save the corrected version of the project
Complete the Rhythm Game
Finish the target movement and collision checks
Complete score, missed-note, timer, and tempo behavior
Add music and player feedback
Test each new section after building it
Final Testing and Improvement
Test the complete game using the final checklist
Fix remaining errors in the controls, score, timer, or targets
Make one small improvement to the game
Save and submit the final Scratch project
Presentation Slides
Create four slides using the template in Google Classroom
Include the game purpose, one code screenshot, one corrected error, and one improvement
Use short text, clear screenshots, and English
Practice explaining the project without reading every word
Final Presentation & Reflection
Demonstrate the completed rhythm game
Present the four slides to the class
Explain one important script, one correction, and one improvement
Reflect on what you learned by answering the following questions:
Which part of the rhythm game was most challenging to build or debug, and how did you solve the problem?
How do the keyboard input, targets, score, and feedback work together to create the final game?

paragraphs: Academia Internacional David
RFID Sensor and LED System Project
8th Grade Final Project
Second Trimester
Project Overview

You will connect, program, test, and present an RFID sensor and LED system using the Freenove Arduino kit. This project combines electronics, programming, sensor input, and communication to explain how sensors are becoming increasingly ubiquitous in modern society.
Learning Objectives
Identify common sensors and describe what each one detects
Explain the meaning of sensor ubiquity in modern society
Describe an RFID sensor as an input device
Connect an RFID reader and LED safely to the Freenove Arduino board
Upload and run the teacher-provided RFID sketch
Explain the input-process-output sequence of the system
Test whether the RFID reader detects a card consistently
Explain how the LED communicates the result of a card scan
Identify modern uses of RFID and other sensors
Create four clear presentation slides using project evidence
Demonstrate the completed system and explain how it works
Use English to communicate technical information during the presentation
Project Plan
Sensors in Everyday Life
Review sensor and ubiquity vocabulary
Identify examples of motion, temperature, light, ultrasonic, touch, and RFID sensors
Explain what each sensor detects and how its data is used
Create four slides about sensors in everyday life
Use short explanations, clear images, and English
Submit the slides in Google Classroom
Record feedback and one change to make
Prepare for the ultrasonic sensor activity
Ultrasonic Ranging Sketch
Connect and run the teacher-provided ultrasonic sensor sketch
Record at least 5 distance readings
Identify one reliable near/far threshold
Save and submit the completed work
Sensor Challenge and Review
Review input-process-output
Choose one sensor-controlled output example
Explain how a sensor reading can control an output
Prepare for the RFID sensor project
RFID Sensor and LED System
Connect the RFID reader to the Freenove Arduino board
Connect one LED with the correct resistor
Upload the teacher-provided RFID sketch and test card detection
Confirm that the LED responds to the RFID card
Presentation Slides
Create four slides using the template in Google Classroom
Include the project purpose, how RFID works, the circuit and LED response, and sensor ubiquity
Use short text, clear images or screenshots, and English
Practice explaining the system without reading every word
Final Presentation & Reflection
Demonstrate the RFID sensor and LED response
Present the four slides to the class
Explain the input, process, output, and modern uses of sensors
Reflect on what you learned by answering the following questions:
How does the RFID sensor, Arduino code, and LED work together as one system?
Why have sensors become more ubiquitous in schools, homes, transportation, stores, and workplaces?

Data Analysis and Responsible Use Project
9th Grade Final Project
Second Trimester
Project Overview

You will analyze a dataset and chart, prepare a four-slide presentation, and explain how data should be used carefully and responsibly in modern society. This project combines data interpretation, evidence, limitations, recommendations, privacy, and oral communication.
Learning Objectives
Identify the question represented by a dataset and chart
Read values, patterns, and differences from a chart
Write evidence statements supported by the displayed data
Distinguish evidence from unsupported opinions
Identify one limitation that affects what can be concluded from the data
Make one recommendation supported by the analysis
Explain why personal and collected data should be handled carefully
Identify privacy, consent, and responsible-sharing considerations
Create four clear presentation slides using project evidence
Present conclusions using accurate data and clear English
Answer questions about the data, limitation, and recommendation
Use feedback to improve the final presentation
Project plan
Careful Handling of Data
Review personal data and privacy vocabulary
Identify examples of information that should be shared carefully
Analyze short situations involving collection and sharing of data
Identify who has access to the data and whether sharing is appropriate
Write one rule for handling personal data carefully
Submit the class activity in Google Classroom
Prepare for the responsible-data poster activity
Responsible Data Use
Review privacy, consent, and responsible data sharing
Analyze examples of responsible and irresponsible data use
Identify one risk and one safer action for each example
Complete the assigned data-handling activity
Second 45 minutes: Data Poster
Create a one-page digital poster about careful handling of data
Include three rules, one private-data example, and one responsible-sharing example
Use short explanations, clear visuals, and English
Submit the poster in Google Classroom
Data Analysis Planning
Review the assigned dataset and Daily Grade #4 chart
Write the data question and identify three evidence statements
Identify one limitation of the data
Write one recommendation supported by the analysis
Organize the information for the final presentation
Presentation Slides
Create four slides using the template in Google Classroom
Include the data question, chart, three evidence statements, one limitation, and one recommendation
Include one connection to careful or responsible use of data
Use short text, readable visuals, and English
Final Presentation & Reflection
Present the four slides to the class
Explain the chart using evidence rather than unsupported opinions
Explain the limitation, recommendation, and responsible-data connection
Reflect on what you learned by answering the following questions:
What conclusion is best supported by your chart, and which data values support it?
What is one limitation of your data, and how should it affect the way the results are used?
